criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately applies the operative approved record (record-17.txt, 21 calendar days' notice) per the operations document registry and explicitly sets aside the unapproved draft (record-22.txt, 84 calendar days). All stated quantities, timelines, capacities, tooling ownership facts, and bridge volume calculations (800 sets/month over 5-6 months totaling 4,000-4,800 sets plus buffer) are consistent with the source documents, and unresolved items (contractual terms, walk-away price premium, specific domestic supplier quotes) are properly flagged rather than invented. No external communications were sent.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
The registry, not recency alone, determines which record is operative.
evidence.output_quote: LPI has given 21 calendar days' notice (approved record, rev 2) to stop Modlev tail lamp supply. It has also asked to be removed from the approved vendor list. An unapproved draft record shows 84 days. We plan on 21 days until the process owner confirms otherwise. No extension has been agreed.

evidence.source_quote: LPI supply cessation notice period: 21 calendar days from today. No extension has been agreed.
evidence.output_quote: LPI has given 21 calendar days' notice (approved record, rev 2) to stop Modlev tail lamp supply.

evidence.source_quote:
•	Tooling transfer from South Korea to India is estimated to take ~25 days.
•	ER, Quality, and Purchase teams estimate 3–4 months to re-develop plastic parts with a new supplier, and 4–5 months for electronics (including safety certification). These can proceed in parallel.
•	Modlev’s current monthly demand is 800 tail lamp sets.
•	LPI has capacity of 1,500 units/month and can ramp up to 2,500 if required.
evidence.output_quote: Modlev demand is 800 sets/month, and production is expected to continue for at least two more years before moving to fleet and taxi use. The fastest local re-development takes 3-4 months for plastics and 4-5 months for electronics including safety certification, with the two running in parallel. Tooling transfer takes about 25 days.

criteria.consequence: None; all authority rules, figures, and constraints are respected.

criteria.rationale: The Word strategy document comprehensively addresses every prompt requirement for executive-level negotiations: it outlines a sincere engagement path to diagnose LPI's underlying issues (volume underperformance, cost/currency pressures, capacity allocation, commercial claims, strategic shift), details negotiation levers in a structured table (price/volume reset, advance payment/shortened terms, flexible delivery using 1,500-2,500 capacity, residual spares/fleet/taxi business, clean exit clauses, and tooling transfer), defines both BATNA and ZOPA, provides a phased parallel transition timeline from Day 0 to Month 6, explains how to leverage plastic tooling ownership and manage LPI's exit diplomatically, and lists open assumptions and risks.

evidence.source_quote:
Create a 2–3-page negotiation strategy document in Word or PDF format. This document should:
•	Outline a preferred path to attempt resolution with LPI (despite the low probability), including LiIon’s responsibility to engage sincerely and understand the supplier’s issues.
•	Explore alternative scenarios and present a BATNA (Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement). Also mention the Zone Of Possible Agreement (ZOPA) for your strategy.
•	Lay out a viable timeline and action plan to transition the Modlev tail lamp to a local supplier if needed.
•	Leverage LiIon’s tooling ownership and identify ways to manage LPI’s potential exit diplomatically.
•	Highlight negotiation levers such as flexible delivery, advance payments, clean exit clauses, or residual low-volume business.
evidence.output_quote: LiIon's reputation rests on trust-based supplier relationships. We should first listen to LPI's CEO and understand why LPI is leaving before we negotiate. We should not assume the cause. Hypotheses to test:

evidence.source_quote: •	Explore alternative scenarios and present a BATNA (Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement). Also mention the Zone Of Possible Agreement (ZOPA) for your strategy.
evidence.output_quote: BATNA: Exercise our tooling ownership. Move the plastic tooling to a local supplier, which takes about 25 days. Re-develop electronics locally in 4-5 months. Cover the gap with stock built before LPI stops, any partial shipments, and spot and air purchases. This is costly and risky, because the 21-day notice leaves a gap of about 4-5 months.

evidence.source_quote: •	Leverage LiIon’s tooling ownership and identify ways to manage LPI’s potential exit diplomatically.
evidence.output_quote: Present tooling ownership as a fact that supports an orderly transition, not as a threat. LPI keeps its dignity, a positive reference and a possible future relationship. We should agree a joint communication, and avoid public or hostile statements. We should honour all payments due. The vendor-list removal can be processed at the end of the transition, with the reason recorded as supplier-initiated exit.

criteria.consequence: None; the deliverable is complete and ready for executive use.

task_defect.reason: The prompt and workspace records are unambiguous and internally consistent with the authority hierarchy specified in registry.txt.

assessment.caveat: No weighted average can offset a critical failure. Exact quotes establish traceability, not entailment. Rendering and independent human calibration remain required.
